status: DESIGN APPENDIX v3 (backlog): rows for milestones M3-M5 and 'post'. Not loaded by the game and not gated by the data test; a row moves into the live file, and under test, when its milestone starts. Rows may reference live ids.
summary: The other 22 conditions: the M3 illnesses and injuries, detailed illnesses (post).
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

conditions.name: Thirst
conditions.signature: dry breathing and a narrowing view
conditions.trade_off: drink the pond now, or walk to a spring or boil it

conditions.name: Frostbite
conditions.signature: numb white fingers or toes that slow the reload or the walk
conditions.trade_off: take off the mitts to set a trap, or wait for a better moment

exposure.accumulate_when: Cold stage very_cold or worse, or air below -10 C with the zone under-insulated

conditions.refreeze_rule: A zone that rewarms and then refreezes worsens one stage (K:28).
conditions.period_view: 'Rub it with snow', slow warming, cold water, then warm soup (K:18).
conditions.game_truth: Gradual rewarming (physick.rewarm) away from the flame, or warm water; rubbing gives no benefit and a 20% chance to worsen frostnip (K:28).

conditions.name: Worms
conditions.signature: a gnawing hunger soon after eating: food lasts a quarter less
conditions.trade_off: pay the surgeon or dose with pinkroot (poison risk), or eat more and live with it
tells: the hunger icon carries a worm pip once incubation ends
an episode of queasiness every few days

cures.note: the surgeon's or the book's remedy (know.worm_remedies)

conditions.period_view: Buchan blames weak digestion, unripe fruit and raw herbs; purges and bitters (K:5).
conditions.game_truth: Intestinal roundworms and tapeworms from raw fish, undercooked game and bad water. Trichinella from bear and pork is a different illness (cond.trichinosis).

conditions.name: Fever and aching after eating bear or pork
conditions.signature: fever and aching muscles: the aim trembles and stamina is short
conditions.trade_off: cook bear and pork through, which costs fuel and time, or risk weeks of weakness

cures.rule: no period cure: time and rest; warm shelter and full meals shorten it by a quarter

conditions.period_view: No one in 1765 could name it: Trichinella was described in 1835 and linked to pork in 1860. People took it for a rheumatic fever or an ague.
conditions.game_truth: Trichinella larvae lodge in muscle; pinkroot and other worm remedies do nothing (N:30, K:31).

conditions.name: Purged
conditions.signature: weak for a day after the surgeon's purge
conditions.trade_off: the cure's price in time

conditions.name: Fever (seasonal)
conditions.note: One seasonal fever replaces ague, chest cold and flux by default (review 2, issue 7). The three detailed conditions stay in the data behind the 'detailed illnesses' setting.

flux.when: bad water, spoiled food, crowded forts in July-August

ague.when: sleeping by marsh or slow water, July-October
ague.signature: fits every two or three game days

chest.when: wet and cold for two or more game hours

conditions.signature: by cause: thirst (flux), fits (ague) or a cough (chest)
conditions.trade_off: keep working the season's best weeks, or rest in a warm shelter and lose them

cures.rule: rest in warm shelter with water and broth halves the duration

conditions.name: Flux (dysentery)
conditions.signature: thirst doubles or trebles
conditions.trade_off: boil every drink, or risk the season's water

cures.rule: hydration kept at 40 or more halves the duration

conditions.period_view: Camp filth and marshes (Pringle); ipecacuanha, rhubarb, opiates, broths (K:7, K:5).
conditions.game_truth: Fluids and broth work; boiled water prevents it.

conditions.name: Scurvy
conditions.signature: weariness, then healing stops
conditions.trade_off: carry dried food light, or carry greens, conifer tea or roots

counter.shown_as: the diet-variety pip in food tooltips and a stage icon from lassitude on

conditions.notes: Spruce beer is weak: fermentation and boiling destroy most vitamin C. Fresh needles hold about 50-100 mg per 100 g, and a Cartier-type infusion about 50 mg (N:29).
conditions.period_view: Lind blamed cold damp lodgings; Amherst ordered spruce beer in 1759 (K:6, K:12).
conditions.game_truth: Vitamin C deficiency; the counter naturally threatens late-winter diets of salt and dried food.

conditions.name: Ague (intermittent fever)
conditions.signature: fits every two or three game days
conditions.trade_off: buy dear Peruvian bark, or work around the fits

conditions.name: Chest cold (catarrh)
conditions.signature: a cough that breaks stealth
conditions.trade_off: hunt anyway and cough, or rest warm

cures.rule: rest in a warm shelter halves the duration

conditions.name: Rheumatism
conditions.signature: stiff joints on cold mornings: slow reloads and draws for two game hours after waking
conditions.trade_off: wade the beaver sets in ice water for the best pelts, or keep your joints

acquire.note: beaver water sets, ice holes, wet camps

conditions.applies: the first 2 game hours after waking when air is below 5 C

course.recurs: each winter once acquired, less with warm dry shelter

cures.rule: warm dry shelter and rest end a flare early

conditions.name: Snow blindness
conditions.signature: burning eyes and a blurred, narrowed view
conditions.trade_off: travel the bright crust at noon, or wear eye shades and travel slower (or at dawn and dusk)

acquire.note: ranging and crust hunting on open snow and lake ice

cures.rule: rest in shade or darkness; a cloth over the eyes

conditions.name: Poisoned
conditions.signature: dizziness and sway
conditions.trade_off: eat an unfamiliar plant when hungry, or identify it first

conditions.name: Burn
conditions.signature: a sore hand for a day
conditions.trade_off: work the fire faster, or safely

conditions.name: Sprain
conditions.signature: a limp and no running
conditions.trade_off: rest a day, or limp home with the load

conditions.name: Broken bone
conditions.signature: a broken limb that takes most of a season
conditions.trade_off: the surgeon's fee, or a crooked mend

conditions.name: Snakebite
conditions.signature: a swollen limb, then dizziness
conditions.trade_off: cross the ledges in summer, or go around

cures.effect: morale text only: 'your faith in the root steadies you'

conditions.name: Wound (shot, arrow, blade, animal)
conditions.signature: bleeding, and a weak limb until it mends
conditions.trade_off: dress it now, or get clear first
conditions.note: Damage itself belongs to the existing hit system (scripts/core/hit.gd); survival owns bleeding, healing and infection.

conditions.name: Infected wound (fever)
conditions.signature: a hot wound and failing strength
conditions.trade_off: the surgeon now, or the poultice and hope

conditions.name: Lingering injury
conditions.signature: weak for two game days after a bad end
conditions.trade_off: the price of dying on Woodsman
conditions.cause: waking after a death on the Woodsman or Hard Winter preset

conditions.name: Camp fever (typhus)
conditions.note: Only during an outbreak event in crowded winter quarters or a jail; closes buildings, raises prices.

conditions.name: Smallpox
conditions.note: A grave world event: towns and forts quarantine, trade stops, councils meet. Player infection is off by default; never a player tool, never shown graphically. Mortality followed war, famine, displacement and crowding, not a 'virgin soil' trait of any people (Kelton; Jones, N:22). For a 1765 start the model is inoculation (variolation) debates in the valley and outbreaks in garrison towns such as Albany; the 1757 Fort William Henry outbreak struck mainly the western, French-allied nations (Steele, N:19) and belongs to the war start (post).
